newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks see-saw as profit taking holds gains.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks see-saw as profit taking holds gains.

text.p: Thai stocks posted gains after opening on Tuesday but profit taking spurred by a lack of change in economic fundamentals caused limited moves up, traders said.
The SET Index had gained 1.01 points, or 0.20 percent, to 505.54 by 0322 GMT. The SET 50 was up 0.23 points to 36.11 in trade worth 933 million baht.

"I think it's most likely profit taking today, I still don't see any good news, and I think liquidity is going to present troubles for some finance companies over the next few days," said a trader at Cathay Capital.
Early trade was volatile as strong opening gains, focused on bank and telecoms issues, pushed the index sharply higher.
But hefty profit taking saw the index sink 4.78 points, or 0.98 percent lower, to 499.75 by 0336 GMT.

Volatility was likely to continue in the near term ahead of today's cabinet meeting and possible developments on new merger rules, the government's budget submission before parliament on Wednesday, and monthly economic data due out on Thursday, traders said.
The Dow's overnight plunge was having little impact on a market dominated by domestic economic concerns, traders said.

Traders said artificial support for the market, indicated by heavy mutual fund buying, may have been partly responsible for Monday's 5.06 percent gains and it could be the fund's intention to hold the index above 500.
Concerns surrounding finance firm stability and loan quality wiped 4.19 percent off finance stocks. by 0352 GMT.
Bangkok Bank Plc was unchanged at 119 baht. Thai Farmers Bank Plc was up 0.50 to 83 and Advanced Info Service Plc rose 13 to 170.
